verdicts.note: 23 years at the office, eight in command, chief deputy under two sheriffs (S1, S2, S5), running on continuity with the retiring sheriff. He has never held elected office, so -1 rather than -2.

'Uphold our laws', recruiting and retention (S1), and proactive, visible deputies with foot patrols (S3). This is enforcement with a community-policing tone, so -1. His refusal to carry out ICE detainer missions (S5, S6) follows state law and is immigration evidence, which does not apply to County, so it does not move safety.

The only support is the 'Disciplined Budgeting' slogan on his priorities page (S3). The same dossier records his main budget argument (S5): the office needs competitive wages that 'current county revenue cannot bridge', so its spending has to grow, funded by economic growth. A justification-for-every-dollar slogan alongside a call for higher payroll is not a clear restraint position. Keep the direction and drop to low.

He runs explicitly on 'it's time for a change at the command staff level' (S3) and leading 'from the front' (S1). He is a 10-year deputy with no command role and has never been elected, but he is an insider in the office, so +1 rather than +2. High holds: the theme is repeated in S1 and S3.

'Holding criminals accountable' (S1) and proactive, 'intelligence-led enforcement' (S2), plus a six-time DUI enforcement award record (S1, S2), are pole_a. Use-of-force reporting and adding victim advocates and code enforcement (S1, S2, S3) are accountability and service additions, not diversion or non-police response, so they do not pull toward pole_b enough to reach 0.
